title: YorvoGate scope status, format 1
description: The answer of GET /_yorvogate/v1/scopes/<name> on a trusted listener (docs/configuration.md#scope-status). With sha256 or absent, the request waited: matched tells whether what it waited for came. A 408 answer has matched false and the current state, which is never the state waited for: treat it as a failure. An answer is open for additions at every level (ADR-0005, amendment 1): a later release may add optional fields within version 1, and values to an open list (x-list: open), so ignore fields you don't know and treat an unknown value of an open list as its general case. A closed list (x-list: closed, here state) gains a value only in a new version. An input format, such as the configuration or a scope file, stays closed.

generation.description: Snapshots of the scope files swapped in since the gate started: information only, not proof that a write is in it.

file_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the scope file the state is about, a refused one included. Absent when there is no file.

state.description: loaded: in effect (its socket open, on a listener with scope sockets). refused: its file isn't valid, or collides, and it holds no claims. reserved: refused, but its last valid claims are held for it. unknown: no scope file.

taken.description: Only when loaded, and only when there are any: the names under the scope's prefixes that another owner's objects have (made before its file was valid). The scope can't create them: an orchestrator should stop before deploying, and decide what to do with the other owner's objects.

kind.description: Open: an unknown kind is a name the scope can't create.

owner.description: scope <name>, or <label>=<value> of an owner no scope has now
